_comment: Every number of docs/benchmarks/figures/*.svg, transcribed from docs/benchmarks.md (the record; this file only repeats it). Sizes in MiB (2^20 bytes), times in ms unless the key says s. Each block names the section of the document, the machine where it matters and the conditions. Sizes are deterministic (for a package version, configuration and numpy) and comparable across runs; times are comparable only within one run.

dataset.name: ICON-CH1 sample
dataset.raw_float32_note: 115 x 1,147,980 x 4 bytes = 528,070,800 bytes = 503.6 MiB (Setup table)

sizes_date6.section: Codec chains; Configuration choices (the defaults row); Physics layer (recipes rows)
sizes_date6.machine: sizes do not depend on the machine; numpy 2.5.4, zarr 3.4.2
sizes_date6.conditions: sample date 6, one date per chunk; rounding: grid and recipe_fit: false unless the row says otherwise; zarr writes without valid dates (forcings lossless); the defaults row (rounding: direct, recipe_fit: true) through the engine without dates (the bytes a zarr write gives, forcings as recipes); the recipes rows from scripts/physics_size.py with dates

rows.label: raw float32
rows.note: computed from the shape, not a store

rows.label: single codec, the defaults (rounding: direct, physics.recipe_fit: true), tree k = 1
single codec with dates (forcings as recipes), tree k = 1
single codec with dates (forcings as recipes), tree_b k = 3

structures.conditions: mean over the 20 sample dates, forcings as recipes, statics referenced, one run; the worst error / bound is 1 / k

physics.conditions: sample date 6 with dates, scripts/physics_size.py, every chunk decoded and checked against the bounds

bench_decode.machine: AMD EPYC 7713, 32 cores reserved, one run
bench_decode.conditions: one real CH1 chunk (date 0 through zarr at the defaults, 31.2 MiB, 115 fields) decoded into a preallocated buffer, 3 interleaved rounds in separate processes (9 decodes per round AVX2, 3 scalar); scripts/bench/bench_decode.py
bench_decode.blosc_note: the Blosc library decodes the same date (298.95 MiB) in about 90 ms on one core and 13-26 ms on 16-32 threads, depending on the run (text, not a table row)

zarr_read.machine: AMD EPYC 7713 (32 cores reserved), gcc 12.3, numpy 2.5.4, zarr 3.4.2, AVX2 kernels
zarr_read.conditions: zarr read of sample date 6 written at the defaults (chains of physics expand without a forcing bound) (a[...], decode and every stage) after two warm-up reads; best / median of 3 rounds of 7, each round and thread count in its own process; Blosc with as many threads; scripts/bench/bench_chain.py

chain_stages.section: Codec chains (where the time goes in the chain)
chain_stages.conditions: chain, tree k = 1, rounding: grid, one profiled read per thread count of an earlier run; the envelope well under 1 ms (not drawn)

stages.stage: static_ref (one write of the 115-field date, single-threaded numpy)

encode.machine: AMD EPYC 7713, 32 cores reserved on a node shared with other jobs, one run
encode.conditions: LatticeCodec.encode of one sample date at the defaults, direct call (no zarr), fitting and verification included; scripts/bench/bench_encode.py; 16 threads: range over the encodes without and with the date; 1 thread: one encode without dates (date 0 is the first encode of the process)

anemoi_create.conditions: anemoi-datasets create (init, load, finalise, patch, cleanup, verify) of sample dates 0-2, tree k = 1, the defaults; wall-clock time of the command; open_dataset + read of the 3 dates in a fresh process, cold, cache off
anemoi_create.codec_part_note: anemoi's own report of the create: 82 s (chain) and 106 s (single codec), most of it loading the source field by field; the rest of the wall-clock time is start-up
